messages.subject: Shiny-application starting error :"An error has occurred The application failed to start."
parts:
Hi,

  While starting shiny application on shiny server i'm getting error like "The application failed to start ,The application exited during initialization",i bit searched in google and follow the steps as per their instructions but still i couldn't able to start my application successfully,kindly help me out.

  Here is my environment : Ubuntu 14.04 LTS
  For error log : please find the attachement .

  I'm using below code in my shiny-server.conf

   # Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
run_as shiny;

# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
  listen 3838;

  # Define a location at the base URL
  location / {

    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server;

    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
  

    # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
    # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
    directory_index on;
  }
}


Note : I can able to start my shiny server .

Thanks,
Manu.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny-application starting error :"An error has occurred The application failed to start."
parts:
Hi, I have the same problem as well, but I found out that the cause of it is due to mixed content between the HTTPS request of the server, and the CSS request from googleapis fonts being in HTTP.
I understand that usually you would need to rename the CSS href to "//" instead of "http://" to resolve this, but I don't know where to do so in Shiny. Would you direct me to the file that converts R to HTML to resolve this issue?
If not, can you direct me to a more straightforward solution to resolve this? Thank you.

Warmest Regards,
Syakyr

messages.subject: Re: Shiny-application starting error :"An error has occurred The application failed to start."
parts:
Just realised the problem after checking the logs, AFTER writing the previous message.
Basically it is due to permissions issues as well as that the shiny user doesn't look at my default directory of R using anaconda, but at /usr/bin/R instead. With that I added a link at /usr/bin/ to link to anaconda's R.
Hope it helps, Manohar.

Warmest Regards,
Syakyr
